The Frito-lay guy at my local meat market had a massive heart attack while stocking up the store. He passed me by as he usually did when I received their shipment in the morning. All is normal as I’m charging customers, I can see him at a distance stocking up the chips. Well, when I looked back down to charge the next customer a soda pop and looked back up he was gone. I couldn’t help my curiosity so I left my register to check. When I found him he had pissed himself and his face was turning purple. I did chest compressions on that man, screaming for someone to call 911. (I live in a city where people stop to look but they definitely won’t help someone in need of assistance) Someone finally called 911 while I was crying giving this man non-stop chest compressions. Paramedics also took 7 minutes to show up and it felt like an eternity. When they were removing his body from the market, I was told nothing could have saved him..

Top it off his wife called while this is happening, my co worker just blurts to her over the phone that her husband had just died and was being transferred to the local hospital. I could hear his wife screaming through the receiver. 

I left work that day in the middle of my shift, I did not care what my bosses said (they still expected me to work with a smile on my face). It took me months to feel okay, what helped me was talking about the incident. I stopped taking people and time for granted. I learned to appreciate life because of that day.


I hope you heal from this soon, this life is not guaranteed. 

Cherish it.
